OpenAI says its new model solved 10 math problems that had remained open for decades

This week, Sam Altman introduced Astra, a new multi-agent system that managed to solve and formally prove 10 difficult mathematical problems, some of which had gone unsolved for decades.

The most impressive part is that Astra didn’t just come up with answers. It translated every proof into Lean, a formal proof language that allows mathematicians to verify each step.

And the cost was surprisingly low: according to OpenAI, solving all ten problems required less than $2,000 worth of tokens at Sol pricing.

Astra works by combining multiple agents that explore different ideas, challenge each other’s reasoning, and gradually build a rigorous proof together.

OpenAI says the system was also tested on other unsolved problems, although it wasn’t able to solve them yet.

The bigger takeaway is that we’re starting to see AI systems move beyond solving textbook exercises and into territory that looks a lot more like real mathematical research.

Astra will also be the first OpenAI model to go through the company’s new government approval process before release.

OpenAI has already published both the research paper and the full Lean proofs. 👀
